Patient presented to services 25 with low mood. Patients family were concerned about lack of personal hygiene and peer relationships. Patient was incredibly involved in housework and did not often leave to visit friends and family. Patient reported little motivation to speak to others or engage in other activities. Patient’s speech was very concise and did not elaborate unless prompted. Patient’s responses did not make sense at times. Patient was prescribed clozapine to deal with these symptoms.
Patient returned to services 3 years later. Some modest improvement in affective symptoms was reported however patient soon stopped taking medication. Patient’s non-adherence was because “the pills contained small robots that could control her brain and her movements, telling her what to do”.  When pushed further about this, patient suggested that talking about this could be dangerous to themselves and to the clinician. Increased dose of sertraline and started patient on chlorpromazine. 
Patient’s contact with reality deteriorated. Patient is talking a lot more than previously, but the words do not make sense logically and jump from topic to topic. Patient has been taken off sertraline and has been prescribed with stelazine adjunct with chlorpromazine. 
Their behaviour is bizarre, and their expressions do not match the content of their speech.  They report taking their medications but believe that the health care service is part of a conspiracy to arrest them. They think that they have discovered a hidden ‘truth’ of the universe, and this makes them dangerous to world leaders around the globe. Therefore, they are being very furtive – which could explain in part their strange clothes and behaviour. They report seeing people following them on the streets, in cafes, etc. They also report hearing ‘secret agents’ discuss how they are going to capture and interrogate the patient – they believe they have ultra-sensitive hearing and that they are picking up on conversations over the radio. Given lack of success with previous antipsychotic medications, patient has been prescribed clozapine with monitoring
Patient has been doing much better and has been reporting for the majority of blood monitoring sessions. There were no ‘red alerts’ during the first 18 months therefore TDM is now less frequent. Patient has started volunteering at a local homeless shelter and is much improved.

Pt is a 32 y/o male who was brought to ER by police after being found wandering on highway at 3am. Pt appeared disheveled and was wearing multiple layers of clothing despite warm weather. On assessment pt was guarded and suspicious, making poor eye contact. Pt endorsed hearing voices which he describes as "the committee" - multiple voices commenting on his actions and sometimes arguing with eachother. Pt reports these voices have been present for approx 8 years but have recently become more instrusive. 
Pt has history of multiple hospitalizations, first occuring at age 22. Poor medication compliance noted - pt states he "doesnt need chemicals" and that the medications "flatten everything out." Pt demonstrates some insight acknowledging he has "mental problems" but denies need for treatment.

MSE: Affect blunted, thought process tangential with occasional derailment. No current SI/HI. Pt started on risperidone 2mg BID.

F/u 6 weeks: Pt attended appt with mother. Some reduction in auditory hallucinations reported tho "the committee" still present at lower volume. Pt tolerating medication reasonably well, reports some drowsiness. Weight gain of 4kg noted - discussed dietary modifications. Risperidone increased to 3mg BID.

F/u 3 months: Pt missed two appointments. When contacted by phone, pt reported discontinuing medication due to sexual side effects (anorgasmia, decreased libido). Voices have returned to baseline. After discussion with pt, switched to aripiprazole 10mg daily.

19 y.o female university student referred by GP following concerns raised by flatmates. Pt reportedly has become increasingly withdrawn over past 6 months, spending most time in room. Flatmates report pt talking to herself and laughing at inappropriate times. Academic performance has declined significantly.

Initial assessment: Pt presents as anxious, fidgeting throughout interview. Speech is soft and latency increased. Pt initially reluctant to discuss symptoms but eventually discloses she has been receiving "messages" through the television that are specifically meant for her. She believes she has been chosen for a special mission but cannot elaborate on what this entails. Denies AVH when asked directly but observed responding to internal stimuli during assessment.

Dx: First episode psychosis - ? prodromal schizophrenia. Bloods and MRI ordered to r/o organic causes. Started on low dose olanzapine 5mg nocte.

09/10/06  Pt attended with mother who has travelled from hometown. Pt showing some improvement - less preoccupied with television messages. Mother reports pt sleeping and eating better. Olanzapine increased to 10mg. Referral made to EIP service.

19/01/2007  Good progress. Pt has returned to some university classes tho taking reduced course load. Delusional beliefs have largely resolved. Pt gaining insight into illness. Continue current treatment. Will monitor for metabolic s/e given olanzapine.

Pt is 45 y/o male with long standing diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia, known to services since age 24. Hx of multiple admissions, longest lasting 14 months. Currently residing in supported accomodation.
Care coordinator concerned re deterioration over past 2 wks. Pt has been refusing to leave room, states neighbors are "pumping gas" into his flat thru the walls. Pt has stuffed towels under doors and taped over air vents. Pt also believes staff at supported accom are poisoning his food - has lost 6kg in past month due to restriced eating.

Pt has been on depot haloperidol decanoate 150mg q4weeks for past 3 years with reasonable stability until now. No recent changes to medication. Possible triggers identified: pt's brother visited 3 weeks ago - relationship historically conflictual.
Increase depot to 200mg. Arrange more frequent visits from care coordinator (2x weekly). Liase with supported accom staff re: meal monitoring. Consider admission if no improvement in 2 weeks.
Pt continues to endorse paranoid delusions about neighbors and staff. Has agreed to voluntary admission for stabilization.
Pt settled on ward after initial agitation. Depot increased to 250mg. Procyclidine 5mg BD added for emerging EPS (mild cogwheeling noted). By day 12, pt showing improvement - engaging in ward activities and eating meals without suspicion. Discharge planning initiated.

28 y/o female, referred urgently by maternity services at 4 weeks postpartum. Pt's husband reports dramatic change in wife's behaviour over past 10 days. Pt sleeping only 1-2 hours per night, pressured speech, and expressing belief that baby has "special powers" and is communicating telepathically with her. Pt presented in elevated mood, talking rapidly and difficult to interupt. Pt dressed brightly with excessive makeup. Pt described grandiose beliefs - states her baby is "the chosen one" and that she has been selected to raise a child who will "save humanity." Pt also expressing paranoid ideas that hospital staff want to take baby away because they know about its special abilities.
Pt has no prior psych history. Family hx significant for bipolar in maternal aunt.

Dx: Postpartum psychosis

Plan: Admission to Mother & Baby Unit. Started on olanzapine 10mg and short course of lorazepam for agitation. Close monitoring of mother-infant interaction.

Pt responding well to treatment. Sleep improved to 6hrs. Grandiose and paranoid beliefs less prominent. Pt bonding well with infant under supervision. Olanzapine increased to 15mg. Significant improvement. Pt gaining insight, describes previous beliefs as "crazy thoughts." Discussing discharge planning with husband. Will continue olanzapine and arrange f/u with perinatal MH team.

52 y/o male with schizoaffective d/o, depressive type. Known to services 20+ years. Currently on clozapine 400mg daily (split dosing - 150mg am, 250mg nocte) with good control of positive symptoms. Pt presents today reporting 6 week history of low mood, anhedonia, and increased sleep (12+ hrs/day). Pt has stopped attending day centre which he previously enjoyed. Pt reports passive SI - "sometimes think everyone would be better off without me" - but denies plan or intent. No active psychotic sx reported, last AVH approx 8 months ago.
Pt appears older than stated age. Poor hygeine noted - body odor, stained clothing. Psychomotor retardation evident. Speech slow, monotonous. Affect constricted, predominantly low. Thought content negative but no delusions elicited. Cognition - pt orientated, though concentration appears impaired.
Clozapine level checked - 420 ng/ml (therapeutic). No recent illness or smoking cessation that might affect levels. WBC and ANC within normal limits.
Add sertraline 50mg daily for depressive episode. Continue clozapine unchanged. Increase CPN visits. Safety plan discussed and documented. Review in 2 weeks - if worsening or active SI develops, consider admission.

2 wk review: Pt reports marginal improvement in mood. SI resolved. Sertraline increased to 100mg. Continue monitoring.

Pt is 38 y/o female with chronic undifferentiated schizophrenia. History of poor treatment response - has trialled risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, and aripiprazole with limited eficacy. Currently on amisulpride 800mg daily. Pt lives with elderly mother who provides significant support with ADLs. Mother accompained pt to todays appt and reports pt continues to experience persistent AVH despite medication. Pt hears voice of deceased father who makes critical comments about her ("you're worthless," "you ruined your mother's life"). Pt also demonstrates significant negative symptoms - avolition, alogia, and flat affect predominate the clinical picture. Pt herself contributed minimally to interview, answering questions with single words or short phrases. When asked about the voices, pt stated "they're always there" with no apparent emotional response. Given inadequate response to multiple antipsychotics, discussed trial of clozapine. Mother expressed concerns about "dangerous blood effects" she had read about online. Spent considerable time explaining monitoring protocol and potential benefits for treatment-resistant cases.
Pre-clozapine workup ordered - FBC, U&E, LFT, lipids, fasting glucose, ECG, CXR. Registration with clozapine monitoring service. Pt and mother provided written information. Will review in 2 weeks to discuss further. Bloods and ECG satisfactory. Pt and mother agreeable to clozapine trial. Titration to begin next week with daily monitoring initially. Amisulpride to be gradually reduced.

24 y/o male brought to A&E by ambulance following bizarre behaviour at a shopping centre. Security staff reported pt was shouting at passersby that they were "demons wearing human skin" and attempted to "exorcise" an elderly woman by placing hands on her head. On assessment pt was highly agitated, required IM haloperidol 10mg and lorazepam 2mg for sedation. Once calmer, pt was interviewed. Pt has fixed belief that demonic entities have invaded Earth and are possessing ordinary people. Pt believes he has been given divine powers to identify and expel these entities. Pt also reports command AVH from "God" instructing him to cleanse the world. Collateral obtained from pts girlfriend (by phone): Pt has been increasingly religous over past 3 months, spending hours reading scripture and watching online videos about spiritual warfare. Pt lost job 6 wks ago after confronting colleague about being "possessed." No prior MH history tho girlfriend notes pt has always been "a bit odd socially."
Urine tox positive for cannabis.

Pt detained under MHA for assessment. Dx: Acute psychotic episode - r/o schizophrenia vs substance-induced psychosis. Plan: Commence olanzapine 10mg, monitor closely, repeat tox screen, obtain collateral from family.

41 y/o male with paranoid schizophrenia, stable on paliperidone depot 150mg q monthly for past 4 years. Pt attends for routine depot and review. Pt reports things are "going ok." Pt continues to live independently in council flat. Pt works part-time as cleaner at local church (arranged through IPS employment service 2 yrs ago). Pt maintains relationship with sister who visits fortnightly. Residual sx: Pt continues to experience intermittent AVH, typically in evenings when alone. Pt describes these as "background noise" that is "annoying but manageable." Pt has developed effective coping strategies - uses headphones to listen to music, calls sister. No delusions elicited. Pt reports good tolerablity of depot. Some weight gain since starting tx (BMI now 29.3) - discussed diet and exercise. Pt attends gym twice weekly. No other s/e reported. Bloods (annual): Fasting glucose 5.8 (slightly elevated), lipids mildly raised, prolactin elevated but asymptomatic. Plan: Continue current depot. Dietary advice reinforced. Repeat fasting glucose in 3/12 - if elevated, consider HbA1c. Continue annual physical health monitoring. Well done to pt on maintaing stability and employment.

67 y/o female with late-onset schizophrenia (onset age 58), referred from CMHT for medication review. Pt has been on trifluoperazine 15mg daily since diagnosis with reasonable symptom control but now experiencing signficant EPS - tardive dyskinesia affecting orofacial region (involuntary tongue movements, lip smacking). Pt continues to experience paranoid beliefs about neighbours spying on her, though less intrusive than previously. Pt reports intermittent AVH - "whispers" that she cannot make out clearly. Pt manages these reasonably well and they do not cause signficant distress. Pt lives alone, widowed 10 years. Has daily contact with daughter who lives nearby. Pt manages ADLs independently tho daughter assists with shopping and finances.
Given TD, plan to cross-taper from trifluoperazine to quetiapine (lower EPS risk). Discussed with pt - she is reluctant to change as "the tablets have worked for years" but accepts need to address involuntary movements which she finds embarassing.
Plan: Commence quetiapine 25mg BD, titrate gradually. Reduce trifluoperazine by 5mg every 2 weeks. Monitor closely for psychotic relapse. AIMS assessment scheduled for 3 months. Daughter to monitor and report any concerns. Cross-taper proceeding. Pt now on quetiapine 100mg BD, trifluoperazine reduced to 5mg. Some mild increase in paranoid thinking noted - pt more suspicious of daughter's motivations. No worsening of AVH. TD unchanged. Continue taper cautiously.
